texto_fonte:
Na Belém dos anos 1930, existiam três possibilidades para quem almejava ingressar no ensino superior: direito, engenharia e medicina. Maria escolheu a terceira opção, mas precisou vencer as objeções das tias. A permissão só foi dada após recorrerem aos conselhos do médico da família. Depois de perguntar para a adolescente se ela realmente queria ser médica, ele fez um alerta: “Você sabe que você vai ter que examinar cadáveres de homens nus?” […]. Ao que ela, segura da escolha que fizera, respondeu: “E daí?”.
Ao permitirem que a filha mais velha, que desde cedo queria ter uma profissão e ganhar a própria vida, decidisse o rumo profissional, os pais de Maria José von Paumgartten Deane (1916-1995) abriram caminho para uma trajetória marcada pelo pioneirismo feminino na ciência e pela melhoria da saúde pública brasileira. A cientista fez importantes contribuições à parasitologia e à medicina tropical, a partir de estudos que ajudaram a elucidar o processo de transmissão e controle da malária, além de avanços nos conhecimentos sobre leishmaniose visceral e doença de Chagas.
O episódio sobre o ingresso na medicina foi relatado por Maria em entrevista concedida em 12 de setembro de 1989, a Flávio Taveira e Rose Goldschmidt, no projeto de história oral Memória de Manguinhos, da Casa de Oswaldo Cruz (COC/Fiocruz). Artigo das documentalistas Laurinda Maciel e Renata Borges, em História, Ciências, Saúde – Manguinhos, apresenta e transcreve parte da conversa, após o neto Camilo Deane Escobar ter assinado um termo de consentimento, em 2024, uma vez que na época em que a entrevista foi concendida a autorização ficou pendente. Ancestralidade do pai e da mãe, estudos, preconceito de gênero, maternidade, questões relacionadas à vida pessoal e profissional ao lado do companheiro, o também parasitologista Leônidas de Mello Deane (1914-1993), foram abordadas no texto.
Projeto de história oral reúne mais de 300 horas de entrevistas
“Maria Deane abriu caminhos. Imagina o que era ser uma mulher e ter uma carreira científica nos anos de 1930, 1940. Ela conseguiu formar herdeiros intelectuais. Quando decidiu dar uma pausa na carreira por causa da maternidade, ela não ficou parada, foi desenvolver outras atividades. Acho que isso mostra a personalidade dela. Era uma pessoa inquieta e que procurava trabalhar em algo que a fizesse feliz”, avalia Laurinda, chamando a atenção para a necessidade de mais arquivos que documentem os feitos de mulheres cientistas e para a relevância de se disseminar o trabalho realizado por elas. “É importantíssimo que elas sejam colocadas em evidência, para que sejam conhecidas pelas novas gerações”.
Leônidas e Maria, em 1937, em expedição científica no Pará (foto: Acervo Fiocruz)
Segundo Laurinda, que é pesquisadora da área de memória, patrimônio cultural e acervos da Casa de Oswaldo Cruz, há outros registros de Maria Deane, além da entrevista, sob a guarda do Departamento de Arquivo e Documentação (DAD) da Casa de Oswaldo Cruz. A Coleção Leônidas e Maria Deane, por exemplo, reúne um material iconográfico que registra a trajetória profissional do casal. O projeto “Memória de Manguinhos”, realizado entre 1986 e 1989, resultou em mais de 300 horas de entrevistas com trinta pesquisadores cujas trajetórias se mostraram fundamentais para a consolidação do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz (IOC).
Filha de pais brasileiros, descendentes de austríacos, portugueses e italianos, Maria nasceu em meio à Primeira Guerra Mundial. Os pais haviam casado por procuração, pois a mãe estava à época em Portugal. “Ela veio para o Brasil num navio cargueiro no qual ela era a única passageira, sob os cuidados diretos do comandante do navio. Então, ela contava que viviam apavoradas com receio de submarinos alemães”, relatou a cientista.
Ao ingressar, em 1932, na Faculdade de Medicina e Cirurgia do Pará, ela integrou uma turma de cerca de sessenta estudantes. Apenas cinco eram mulheres e todas se chamavam Maria. Ao longo do curso, foram aceitas pelos colegas, mas “alguns professores” alfinetavam com frases como “Ah, mulher, devia estar em casa, coando café”.
No trabalho de campo, Maria era a única mulher entre os pesquisadores
Foi na medicina que Maria conheceu Leônidas, “dois anos mais velho e dois anos mais adiantado”, com quem viria a dividir a casa, o laboratório e as pesquisas de campo, uma parceria que os fez serem conhecidos no meio científico como “os Deane”. A carreira dela e de Leônidas se “misturaram” muito, disse. Juntos, dedicaram-se a endemias que assolavam o país e se tornaram conhecidos internacionalmente.
Maria e Leônidas integraram a equipe do cientista Evandro Chagas (1905-1940), que, fora encarregado pelo pai, Carlos Chagas (1878-1934), de investigar uma nova doença, a leishmaniose visceral, identificada no Brasil em 1934. O filho iniciou as pesquisas em 1936, como chefe da Comissão Encarregada do Estudo da Leishmaniose Visceral Americana, e, em 1937, criou o Serviço de Estudos de Grandes Endemias.
Maria durante excursão do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz ao Noroeste do Brasil, em 1938 (foto: Acervo Fiocruz)
O casal se embrenhou nas matas de Abaeté, na região amazônica, em expedições científicas que duravam semanas, em busca de casos de leishmaniose visceral. Maria era a única mulher do grupo, constituído por pesquisadores do Instituto de Patologia Experimental do Norte e do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz (IOC):
“Aí que eu fui sentir um pouco o problema de ser mulher em certas circunstâncias, não na família, que já estava acostumada com o meu comportamento um pouco independente, e também não do grupo de trabalho, que me aceitou muito bem. Mas, na época, achavam que mulher num grupo só de homem… eu nunca liguei para essas coisas, mas sabia”, contou. Nas incursões na floresta amazônica, viveu “situações bastante complicadas” e gratificantes. “Foi um tempo realmente muito gostoso […] de descobertas, não descobertas, mas “descobertinhas”, digamos. De vida, de Brasil, de trabalho, a sensação de que a gente estava fazendo alguma coisa que podia ser útil, se bem que depois a gente fica pensando no que é útil mesmo”.
A cientista chegou a iniciar o Curso de Aplicação do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz, onde convivia com pessoas que faziam parte de seus estudos e leitura, mas deixou o curso e foi para o Nordeste quando eclodiu uma epidemia de malária na região. Ela e Leônidas acabaram se desentendendo com Evandro e decidiram fazer parte de outro projeto, o da Fundação Rockefeller, após um convite de Frederick Soper (1893-1977), que dirigia o Serviço Cooperativo de Febre Amarela da Fundação Rockefeller. “Nós saímos… hoje nós lamentamos muito, mas tolices, bobagens…”, relatou na entrevista. O casal foi trabalhar no Serviço de Malária do Nordeste, reforçando o combate ao Anopheles gambiae, mosquito transmissor da malária. Logo depois, Evandro morreria, em um acidente de avião, em 1940, poucos dias após o casamento de Leônidas e Maria Deane.
Mais uma vez, Maria Deane trabalhou em “um universo totalmente masculino”. Embora se sentisse “à vontade”, havia comentários sobre seu salário, “maior do que os vários homens”. “A minha posição em relação a esses problemas é a seguinte: existe discriminação contra a mulher em todos os meios, existe mesmo, a gente sabe, não adianta querer negar (…) Esse sentimento de superioridade masculina é uma coisa tão arraigada na sociedade, tão antiga, que você não pode pensar que, de um momento para o outro, você vai mudar, não pode esperar isso aí”.
Quando a filha nasceu, Maria Deane deu um tempo na carreira. Sobre a parada temporária, afirmou ter sido uma escolha e frisou não ser intolerante em relação ao tema: “Eu acho que as pessoas têm uma certa liberdade de viver sua vida como bem lhes pareça, desde que não chateiem os outros”. Mas observou que o trabalho feminino poderia ajudar a sustentar a família e fez um questionamento: “Por que não dar à mulher a oportunidade de realmente empregar os seus talentos, a sua inteligência em alguma coisa, mais do que só mexer panela, ora veja, por que não?”. A interrupção prejudicou em parte a carreira, ela admitiu. Embora tenha dado aulas em cursos de pós-graduação e feito trabalhos de tradução durante o período, não pode se dedicar às pesquisas e nem publicar artigos.
Maria Deane, em seu laboratório do Departamento de Protozoologia do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz,, com Leônidas Deane, em 1992 (foto: Acervo Fiocruz)
Em 1942, após o encerramento do Serviço de Malária do Nordeste, os dois foram contratados como médicos assistentes pelo Serviço Especial de Saúde Pública (Sesp) e alocados no Instituto Evandro Chagas, em Belém, onde trabalharam com malária e filariose. Mais adiante, já vinculados à Universidade de São Paulo (USP), o casal foi cedido à Campanha de Erradicação da Malária (CEM). Em razão disso, a partir de outubro de 1958, eles moraram cerca de um ano no Rio de Janeiro, onde as atividades eram sediadas. O casal foi responsável pela organização do Laboratório Central da campanha. Ao retornarem, Maria Deane foi para o Instituto de Medicina Tropical de São Paulo (IMTSP), criado em 1959, e vinculado à Faculdade de Medicina da USP nos primeiros tempos.
Após o golpe de 1964, o casal viveu um período difícil. A filha participava ativamente da política universitária e acabou perseguida pela ditadura. No início da década de 1970, o casal se exilou inicialmente em Portugal, e, depois, na Venezuela. “Foi uma época muito dura, muito dura mesmo, para ela e para nós”. Luisa foi para a Argentina, mas acabou presa em razão da ditadura que se instalou, após o golpe militar de 1976. Na entrevista, Maria fala sobre o apoio da polícia brasileira, que negou o visto para Luisa retornar ao país. “Depois ela foi presa. Nós fizemos um processo que foi até o Supremo Tribunal Militar e lá mantiveram a negativa de dar o visto [risos]. Porque ela era um elemento muito perigoso, depois, passada a história, a gente acha até graça. Então, um filho seu, que você está acostumado, pessoa generosa, bondosa e tudo, que não podia ver um animal maltratado… é muito perigosa […]”.
Na década de 1980, ela e Leônidas ingressaram no Instituto Oswaldo Cruz (IOC), como pesquisadores do Departamento de Protozoologia, que mais tarde ela viria a chefiar. Em 1984, a cientista descreveu o duplo ciclo do agente etiológico da doença de Chagas, Trypanosoma cruzi, em gambás, considerado o mais antigo reservatório do parasito, em áreas livres de barbeiros em domicílio. Mais adiante, em 1986, foi eleita vice-diretora do IOC e, dois anos depois, contribuiu com a reestruturação da pós-graduação da unidade. Em 2001, a Fiocruz homenageou os Deane nomeando a unidade de Manaus como Centro de Pesquisa Leônidas e Maria Deane, atual Instituto Leônidas & Maria Deane – Fiocruz Amazônia.

candidato.titulo: New database iCellOmics integrates multiomics data for industrial cell lines
candidato.resumo: Industrially relevant cell lines include both direct production hosts for recombinant proteins, vaccines and viral vectors, and biomedical models that serve as references for host-cell engineering and comparative studies. These cell lines support the development and worldwide supply of recombinant therapeutics, viral vaccines and gene therapies.

texto_fonte:
New database iCellOmics integrates multiomics data for industrial cell lines
Industrially relevant cell lines include both direct production hosts for recombinant proteins, vaccines and viral vectors, and biomedical models that serve as references for host-cell engineering and comparative studies. These cell lines support the development and worldwide supply of recombinant therapeutics, viral vaccines and gene therapies.
However, their genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles, along with phenotype information extracted from scientific literature, remain scattered across different repositories, projects and publications. Differences in reference genomes and analytical workflows further complicate data integration, making it difficult to systematically characterize these cell lines.
The National Genomics Data Center (NGDC), part of the China National Center for Bioinformation (CNCB), has released iCellOmics, an open-access multiomics database for industrial cell lines. The work was published online in Nucleic Acids Research on Nov. 10.
According to the researchers, this work integrates, for the first time, multiomics data and literature-curated gene–phenotype knowledge for multiple industrially relevant cell lines within a unified data analysis framework, addressing the lack of resources for integrated multiomics analysis across industrial cell lines.
The current release of iCellOmics covers 17 industrially relevant cell lines and integrates six data categories: reference genomes and annotation information for seven species, encompassing 144,018 protein-coding genes; 170,408,888 genomic variants with functional annotations from 55 whole-genome sequencing projects across 15 cell lines; 673 differential-expression comparisons from 241 bulk transcriptome sequencing projects; 1,047,274 cells from 30 single-cell transcriptome sequencing projects; 287,089,415 chromatin-accessibility peaks from 171 ATAC-seq projects; and 37,213 gene–phenotype relationships extracted from 6,312 publications, involving 6,605 gene/protein entities and spanning 104 standardized phenotype subcategories.
iCellOmics supports both "cell line-centric" data browsing and "gene-centric" cross-omics retrieval. Users can browse the available data across different modules by cell line or use the Gene Search function to retrieve an integrated profile of a specific gene in a given cell line. This profile covers variant sites, expression comparisons, accessible chromatin regions, an overview of single-cell transcriptome data and gene–phenotype relationships extracted from the literature.
The database also organizes literature-curated gene–phenotype relationships into an interactive knowledge graph, with switchable detailed and collapsed views. Users can filter the graph by cell line, phenotype category, entity name, relationship type and PubMed ID. For each relationship, the database displays relevant literature context, experimental perturbations and reported effects, offering knowledge-guided support for host-cell engineering.
In addition, iCellOmics integrates the JBrowse 2 genome browser and online GO/KEGG enrichment analysis tools. It also provides downloadable processed datasets covering reference genomes, chromatin accessibility and single-cell transcriptomes, facilitating local analyses.
Overall, the multiomics data and gene–phenotype knowledge available through iCellOmics provide valuable resources for basic research and support the engineering of industrial cell lines, as well as the development and optimization of high-yield, stable producer cell lines.
Publication details
Xiaojing Gao et al., iCellOmics: connecting multi-omics profiles and phenotype evidence across industrially relevant cell lines, Nucleic Acids Research (2026). DOI: 10.1093/nar/gkag1148

candidato.titulo: Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid lands first non-automotive trial
candidato.resumo: Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid robot will undergo its first trials outside the automotive industry at a major semiconductor manufacturer in early 2027. The post Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid lands first non-automotive trial appeared first on The Robot Report .

texto_fonte:
GlobalFoundries, a leading semiconductor manufacturer, will become the first customer outside of the automotive industry to test Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid. Atlas testing will begin in early 2027, marking a key step in Boston Dynamics’ efforts to commercialize its humanoid.
GlobalFoundries is already a customer of Boston Dynamics, having deployed its Spot quadruped for industrial inspections for several years. The companies are expanding that relationship to include additional Spot deployments across GlobalFoundries’ global manufacturing network. Since April 2026, two Spot robots at its Singapore facility have collectively traveled nearly 900 km (559 mi.) and completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas, achieving a 99% mission success rate, according to the companies.
Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries will identify potential humanoid applications in semiconductor manufacturing, assess integration requirements and customer readiness, and begin training Atlas to perform specific tasks. The companies did not disclose how many Atlas robots will be involved, which facilities will host the humanoids, or what initial tasks they will perform.
The Robot Report has reached out to Boston Dynamics for additional information. This story will be updated if we learn new information.
The agreement gives Boston Dynamics an opportunity to validate Atlas in a manufacturing environment outside of that of its parent company, Hyundai Motor Group. While automotive manufacturing has emerged as an early proving ground for humanoids, semiconductor manufacturing could present a different set of technical and operational requirements.
“Spot has helped us shift from reactive to predictive maintenance, collecting data across thousands of inspection points to prevent downtime and keep our fabs running more efficiently,” said Pradip Singh, chief manufacturing officer at GlobalFoundries. “Scaling Spot and testing Atlas are the next steps in our journey to AI-enabled manufacturing, putting physical AI to work across our operations worldwide.”
Boston Dynamics expands Atlas beyond Hyundai
When Boston Dynamics unveiled the product version of its electric Atlas humanoid at CES 2026, it said its initial production run for the year was fully committed. The humanoids were earmarked for Hyundai and Google DeepMind, the latter of which is working with Boston Dynamics to integrate its Gemini Robotics foundation models into Atlas.
Boston Dynamics said at the time it planned to begin working with additional customers in early 2027. GlobalFoundries represents the first publicly announced manufacturing customer outside of Hyundai Motor Group.
In September, Boston Dynamics opened its Robotics Metaplant Application Center (RMAC) at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America near Savannah, Ga. The facility serves as a training and testing ground for Atlas ahead of its integration into Hyundai’s automotive manufacturing operations.
Atlas is initially being trained to perform parts sequencing and material handling tasks, with Hyundai targeting component assembly applications by 2030. Boston Dynamics plans to move the RMAC into a facility approximately 10 times its current size in 2027.
Hyundai has outlined plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas humanoids across Hyundai Motor and Kia manufacturing facilities over the next several years. It also plans to establish a U.S. factory capable of producing 30,000 robots annually.
Boston Dynamics has ambitions for Atlas well beyond automotive manufacturing. In September, the company said it was in discussions with existing Spot and Stretch customers across several industries, including aerospace, semiconductors, logistics, food and beverage, and life sciences.
Boston Dynamics’ installed base of mobile robots could provide it with an advantage over humanoid developers that are still establishing relationships with industrial customers. Those existing relationships give Boston Dynamics access to facilities, operational data, and customers that already have experience integrating autonomous robots into their workflows.
Atlas continues to evolve
Despite entering early production, Atlas continues to undergo hardware and software development. Boston Dynamics unveiled in October a redesigned hand for Atlas featuring four fingers and 13 degrees of freedom (DoF), up from seven DoF in its previous three-fingered design.
Boston Dynamics designed the new hand with directly actuated joints and with simulation-based reinforcement learning in mind. The redesign is intended to improve the robot’s dexterity while balancing the reliability and manufacturability requirements of an industrial robot.
Boston Dynamics also demonstrated an experimental version of Atlas equipped with wheels in place of its feet. Rather than signaling the development of a new commercial product, the experiment served as a testbed for whole-body control and demonstrated the ability of reinforcement learning-based control policies to adapt to changes in the robot’s hardware.
The GlobalFoundries announcement comes just over a month after Boston Dynamics appointed former Amazon executive Rohit Prasad as CEO. Prasad previously served as senior vice president and head scientist for Alexa and artificial general intelligence at Amazon, where he helped build Alexa and led the development of the Amazon Nova family of foundation models. His appointment comes as Boston Dynamics looks to accelerate the integration of AI into its robots.

texto_fonte:
Microsoft eleva desempenho do Xbox Series em até 16% com tecnologia do Steam Deck
Por Raphael Giannotti |
A Microsoft começou a testar uma nova ferramenta que promete extrair ainda mais performance dos consoles Xbox Series X|S sem exigir mudanças no hardware. De acordo com a documentação oficial da atualização de outubro de 2026 do Microsoft Game Development Kit (GDK), a empresa introduziu de forma experimental o compilador de shaders ACO, originalmente desenvolvido pela comunidade de código aberto do projeto Mesa e amplamente utilizado no Linux e no Steam Deck para GPUs AMD.
Nos testes iniciais feitos pelo próprio Xbox junto aos estúdios parceiros, o novo compilador entregou ganhos de desempenho que variam entre 2% e 16% em tempo de execução, dependendo do motor gráfico, do tipo de conteúdo e dos gargalos de shaders de cada jogo. Além de melhorar a taxa de quadros e a eficiência da GPU RDNA 2 dos consoles, a tecnologia também acelera o próprio processo de compilação durante o desenvolvimento.
Otimização extra junto com a chegada do FSR 4
A adoção do compilador baseado em ACO funciona como uma alternativa opcional ao compilador padrão tradicional do Xbox, permitindo que os desenvolvedores otimizem o código executado diretamente nos chips gráficos da AMD. Como o ACO foi projetado especificamente para arquiteturas Radeon modernas, ele tende a gerar instruções mais enxutas e melhor gerenciamento de registradores do que soluções genéricas.
A novidade chega na mesma atualização do GDK que também trouxe suporte oficial ao AMD FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 para os consoles da geração atual, incluindo os modelos INT8 otimizados para a arquitetura RDNA 2 do Xbox Series X|S. Somadas, as duas tecnologias dão aos estúdios ferramentas importantes para elevar a qualidade visual e a estabilidade de desempenho dos jogos na reta final da atual geração.
Em se tratando do futuro da divisão Xbox, a empresa disse que o próximo console irá além e atuará também como hardware que rodará jogos de PC.

candidato.titulo: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return as Nvidia CEO
candidato.resumo: In his first statement since his resignation, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed openness to returning to his former role.

texto_fonte:
Jensen Huang, the former CEO of Nvidia who resigned last week amid the fallout from two extramarital affairs, said in his first public statement since abdicating his position that he would be willing to return to the corner office at the company he co-founded.
"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a statement posted on X. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
Huang has seen public support from other tech founders and CEOs, such as SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick. They and some investors and Nvidia employees signed an online petition and have continued to be vocal on social media, namely Musk's X. President Donald Trump also said that he "would not mind" Huang's return.
Huang resigned on Thursday following two scandals: one affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed believed by some US Intelligence officials to be a potential Chinese government asset; and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care and Huang's direct report.
Despite Huang's apparent willingness to return, Nvidia's board doesn't seem likely to make that move. Reports yesterday claim that the board is more focused on its ongoing investigation into Huang's affairs and a national security inquiry and is not considering Huang's return. texto_fonte:
November 17, 2026
NASA’s NICER Telescope Ends Science Operations
After studying the universe for six and a half years beyond its initial mission, NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) telescope on the International Space Station has ended science operations.
The mission and space station teams are now focused on plans to finalize NICER’s 8-year archive of X-ray science observations and decommission and detach the telescope from its perch near the station’s starboard solar array.
In June 2025, NICER was suddenly unable to swivel side-to-side beyond its current orientation, which limited its ability to track cosmic objects. The team paused data collection to investigate the issue.
Robotic cameras on the outside of the station collected photographs of NICER that helped eliminate external causes. After an extensive investigation, engineers think an internal motor has failed, limiting the telescope’s motion.
Launched in 2017, NICER embarked on an initial 18-month prime mission. Since then, it has made groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars, which contain the densest matter in the universe that we can measure, and revolutionized our understanding of black holes, active galaxies, and other mysterious phenomena in our universe.
The telescope also successfully demonstrated the potential of pulsar-based spacecraft navigation in X-rays that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond. Closer to home, technology developed to test NICER before launch is being incorporated into prototype portable CT scanners, materials analysis systems, and other applications.
August 5, 2025
Science Observations Remain Paused for NASA’s NICER Telescope
Science operations by NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer), an X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, remain paused as the team continues to evaluate the telescope’s systems after an issue developed with one of its motors. The motor is unable to move NICER beyond its current position side to side, and the telescope’s status has not changed since operations were halted June 17.
The primary goal is to move NICER into its stowed configuration in case it needs to accommodate space station activities, though the current placement does not pose a safety issue to the station or crew. The team currently does not have a timeframe for returning to science operations.
Photos taken by robotic cameras outside the station are helping eliminate external causes for the issue. Now the team is coordinating with space station personnel to perform troubleshooting maneuvers and determine potential causes within the payload.
Since it began observing the X-ray universe in 2017, NICER has successfully demonstrated a form of deep space navigation that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond.
Designed for a prime mission of 18 months and now in its eighth year of operations, NICER has made groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars, which contain the densest matter in the universe that we can measure, and revolutionized our understanding of black holes, active galaxies, and other mysterious phenomena in our universe. Technology developed to test NICER before launch is being incorporated into prototype portable CT scanners, communications systems, and several other applications on Earth for the benefit of all.
June 24, 2025
NASA’s NICER Telescope Suspends Science Operations
NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer), an X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, has paused observations due to a problem with one of the motors that drives its ability to track cosmic objects.
The NICER team paused operations June 17 when performance degradation in the motor began affecting science observations. Engineers are investigating the cause and potential solutions.
The telescope was installed near the space station’s starboard solar array in 2017. The NICER mission has successfully demonstrated a form of deep space navigation that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond. It has also made groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars, which contain the densest matter in the universe that we can measure, and revolutionized our understanding of black holes, active galaxies, and other mysterious phenomena in our universe.
April 17, 2025
Following Repair, NASA’s NICER Improves Daytime Measurements
A NASA X-ray telescope on the International Space Station called NICER, or Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer, has regained additional daytime observation capabilities thanks to repairs completed during a spacewalk and a reconfiguration of its detectors.
In May 2023, NICER developed a light leak in which unwanted sunlight began entering the instrument. Photos taken from inside the space station revealed several small areas of damage to the telescope’s thin thermal shields, which block sunlight while allowing X-rays through to the detectors. Nighttime observations were unaffected, and with operational adjustments, the NICER team was able to recover about 20% of station daytime observations.
In January, NASA astronaut Nick Hague installed nine patches to cover the largest areas of damage during a spacewalk. After resuming science operations, the NICER team determined the overall level of sunlight inside NICER had substantially reduced. Still, it experienced more visible-light interference than expected.
Close-up, high-resolution photos from the spacewalk allowed the team to see additional small holes and cracks in the thermal shields that were not previously visible. These accounted for the remaining sunlight intrusion.
After further analysis, the NICER team developed a novel approach to regaining additional daytime data collection.
Each X-ray that hits a NICER detector generates electrical charge that is sensed by a measurement/power unit (MPU). After so many hits, the detector resets — like emptying a cup before it overflows.
Sunlight can also create charge that accumulates in the detector, adding water to the metaphorical cup. There was so much sunlight entering NICER that the detectors were filling up with charge and resetting thousands of times for every X-ray detection. It overwhelmed the MPU’s ability to process the valid X-ray events.
Hague’s repair in January reduced the amount of sunlight entering NICER, which enabled the team to reconfigure the MPUs to ignore the sunlight-generated resets. After initial testing on the ground, the team updated one MPU before switching all seven. The changeover was completed March 12.
In combination with the patches, the reconfiguration has allowed NICER to return to collecting observations during more than 70% of station daytime, as the telescope continues to help us better understand the X-ray universe, including neutron stars, black holes, and other energetic phenomena. The team continues to look for more opportunities to improve NICER’s operations.
Jan. 24, 2025
NASA’s NICER Continues Science Operations Post Repair
NASA crew aboard the International Space Station installed patches to the agency’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) mission during a spacewalk on Jan. 16. NICER, an X-ray telescope perched near the station’s starboard solar array, resumed science operations later the same day.
The patches cover areas of NICER’s thermal shields where damage was discovered in May 2023. These thin filters block sunlight while allowing X-rays to pass through. After the discovery, the NICER team restricted their observations during the station’s daytime to avoid overwhelming the mission’s sensitive detectors. Nighttime observations were unaffected, and the team was able to continue collecting data for the science community to make groundbreaking measurements using the instrument’s full capabilities.
The repair went according to plan. Data since collected shows the detectors behind the patched areas are performing better than before during station night, and the overall level of sunlight inside NICER during the daytime is reduced substantially.
While NICER experiences less interference from sunlight than before, after analyzing initial data, the team has determined the telescope still experiences more interference than expected. The installed patches cover areas of known damage identified using astronomical observations and from photos taken by both external robotic cameras and astronauts inside the space station. Measurements collected since the repair and close-up, high-resolution photos obtained during the spacewalk are providing new information that may point the way toward further daytime data collection.
In the meantime, NICER continues operations with its full measurement capabilities during orbit night to enable further trailblazing discoveries in time domain and multimessenger astrophysics.
June 8, 2023
Sunlight ‘Leak’ Impacting NASA’s NICER Telescope, Science Continues
On Tuesday, May 22, NASA’s NICER (Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer), an X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, developed a “light leak,” in which unwanted sunlight enters the instrument. While analyzing incoming data since then, the team identified an impact to daytime observations. Nighttime observations seem to be unaffected.
The team suspects that at least one of the thin thermal shields on NICER’s 56 X-ray Concentrators has been damaged, allowing sunlight to reach its sensitive detectors.
To mitigate the effects on measurements, the NICER team has limited daytime observations to objects far away from the Sun’s position in the sky. The team has also updated commands to NICER that automatically lower its sensitivity during the orbital day to reduce the effects from sunlight contamination. The team is evaluating these changes and assessing additional measures to reduce the impact on science observations.
To date, more than 300 scientific papers have used NICER observations, and the team is confident that NICER will continue to produce world-class science.

candidato.titulo: SAXON Q Announces ‘Quantum Watchdog,’ to Detect When Quantum Computers Fail
candidato.resumo: Insider Brief PRESS RELEASE — SAXON Q, a leader in NV-center quantum computing, today announced the Quantum Watchdog, a patented safety system that monitors a quantum computer and puts it into a safe mode if it fails. The system is designed for quantum computers operating in research environments and upcoming industrial applications — including robotics, […]

texto_fonte:
Insider Brief
- SAXON Q announced Quantum Watchdog, a patented system designed to detect quantum computer hardware failures and trigger protective responses, with implementation available in early 2027.
- The system uses an independent classical processor to run verified test calculations, monitor operating conditions and compare results across multiple quantum processors.
- Custom configurations can devote up to half of processing time to safety checks, while fully certified versions are expected within the next few years.
PRESS RELEASE — SAXON Q, a leader in NV-center quantum computing, today announced the Quantum Watchdog, a patented safety system that monitors a quantum computer and puts it into a safe mode if it fails. The system is designed for quantum computers operating in research environments and upcoming industrial applications — including robotics, health care, automotive and defense — where hardware failures could put people or equipment at risk
SAXON Q’s Quantum Watchdog runs on its own classical processor, with a separate clock, timers and sensors. Its firmware holds a library of test calculations, along with the statistics to tell if the quantum computer isn’t behaving within set parameters. The watchdog can then respond as needed to protect the processors and operations. Each system will be custom-built, giving customers control over how much monitoring they need. The watchdog is designed to work across quantum computing modalities, from data center clusters to room-temperature systems headed for use in the field.
“Quantum computers are already doing valuable work in data centers and labs today, and room-temperature systems like ours will take them places others can’t, from vehicles and robots to defense systems in the field,” said Bernd Burchard, co-founder and chief intellectual property officer of SAXON Q. “Either way, a failure has real consequences. We designed the Quantum Watchdog to make it possible to bring quantum computers into security and safety-related areas while minimizing the risk to people and property.”
Safety systems for classical electronics and computers have been around for decades, and frequently work by double-checking results. But checking a quantum computer’s answers isn’t always practical, and it doesn’t reveal whether the hardware itself is starting to fail. SAXON Q’s Quantum Watchdog takes a different approach, thanks to advancements in compact, multi-core quantum processors that can check each other’s work.
Instead of checking every result, Quantum Watchdog confirms that the quantum computer itself is working as expected. While in service, it periodically swaps a user’s calculation for a test problem that has a verified answer. If the machine returns the wrong answer more often than it should, the watchdog marks it as a failure. It also tracks physical operating conditions, including power draw, temperature and magnetic field. If any fall outside the preset limits, the watchdog treats it as a failure and reacts according to established protocols.
If a machine is running multiple quantum processors, the watchdog takes a page from aircraft and electronic brake systems that rely on redundancies. For a unit running two processors, it will test both and compare the answers, then put the unit into safe mode if the answers don’t match. With three processors or more, the watchdog takes a vote and can then shut down the processors that come back with answers that don’t match the majority to keep the others operating.
“While the quantum industry is actively building toward error correction, there’s still the problem of making sure the hardware itself is working properly,” said Marius Grundmann, co-founder and CEO of SAXON Q. “A hardware failure is typically the result of an actual defect from manufacturing flaws, aging or tampering. That matters more and more as room-temperature machines like ours leave the lab. Error correction handles errors, the watchdog catches failures.”
Quantum Watchdog is designed and patented as a hardware-neutral solution. It can be applied to quantum computing modalities including superconducting and trapped-ion processors, along with other qubit platforms and quantum sensors. The watchdog was initially developed, however, with NV-center diamond processors in mind, including SAXON Q’s room-temperature, multi-core quantum computers. For industries that operate outside the lab and can benefit from the power of quantum computing, that opens up a host of possibilities.
Earlier this year, SAXON Q announced two new multi-core quantum computers, the SXQ128 and the SXQ512. In either model, one of the system’s control circuits can be configured as a Quantum Watchdog at the customer’s request, trading some computing capacity for added protection. SAXON Q is currently focusing on quantum HPC clusters where operators need to be able to identify and swap out a failed machine while the rest of the cluster continues to run, and on defense, where systems need to operate without cloud access.
Availability
SAXON Q’s Quantum Watchdog will be available for implementation in early 2027, and will be available upon request. Each watchdog is custom built based on individual requirements. For users needing the highest levels of safety, up to half of a quantum computer’s processing time can be spent on test calculations, while less critical operations can be set to test only at startup or intermittently.
A basic version of the watchdog that does not require industry certification takes around six months to implement. A fully certified version that meets the highest safety requirements — including independent audits and field testing — will be available within the next few years. Patents have been granted in Europe, the U.S. and China, and SAXON Q is now offering licenses to quantum hardware manufacturers, system integrators and OEMs.
Matt Swayne

candidato.titulo: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
candidato.resumo: Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal. "Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me […]

texto_fonte:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.
Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
‘I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,’ Huang said.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.
“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”
More than 193,000 people, including CEOs like Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, have signed a letter to “bring Jensen back.” President Trump has also been supportive of Huang returning as CEO, saying yesterday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea.” (Trump had earlier tossed out former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a potential replacement.) On Monday, Nvidia’s board reportedly was “not considering” having Huang return, and today, CNN reported that the board is “not considering reinstating Huang.”
Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
Here is Huang’s full statement:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen
Update, November 17th: CNN reports that Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating Huang.

Jensen

There’s also significant resistance to the idea in Congress, where Huang still faces significant questions about his role in chip exports to China-linked firms.
Reached by Politico, one senator called Huang’s reinstatement “one of the worst ideas I’ve heard today.”

candidato.titulo: Solar-powered radiation detector for use in disaster zones
candidato.resumo: A portable, solar-powered radiation detector is described in the International Journal of Energy Technology and Policy. The device was designed to operate continuously without utility power, potentially improving radiation monitoring in remote areas and disaster zones when and where an external power supply is unavailable.

texto_fonte:
Solar-powered radiation detector for use in disaster zones
A portable, solar-powered radiation detector is described in the International Journal of Energy Technology and Policy. The device was designed to operate continuously without utility power, potentially improving radiation monitoring in remote areas and disaster zones when and where an external power supply is unavailable.
The system combines solar panels with rechargeable lithium batteries, drawing power from sunlight while storing energy for periods of low illumination or power loss. Tests demonstrated 24 hours of uninterrupted operation under illumination of 200 lux, a relatively low light level. The device also supports USB fast charging for times when there is access to power.
The detector uses a Geiger-Müller (GM) tube, a sensor that detects ionizing radiation, including gamma and beta radiation. It uses a dynamic threshold algorithm to adjust the level at which an alarm is triggered, reducing false alarms by 30%, according to the researchers.
This novel device addresses a limitation of conventional portable detectors, which usually need an external electricity supply or have restricted battery life. Continuous operation during power failures could prove particularly valuable following earthquakes and nuclear accidents, when infrastructure may be damaged. Fundamentally, the device makes radiation monitoring accessible and less dependent on established infrastructure.
The researchers argue that the relatively simple design, using established electronic components, should allow affordable mass production, which could open up a putative market for a home device that one might add to a household emergency kit along with one's clockwork radio, rechargeable flashlight, battery packs and other equipment one might need in a future emergency situation.
More information
Weizhe Li et al., Design of solar-powered nuclear radiation instrument, International Journal of Energy Technology and Policy (2026). DOI: 10.1504/ijetp.2026.157557

candidato.resumo: Em julgamento realizado nesta segunda-feira (16), o hacker responsável pelo vazamento de GTA 6 em 2022 , Arion Kurtaj, declarou-se culpado por invadir e vazar clipes inacabados, além de tentar extorquir a Rockstar. Ele fazia parte do grupo hacker conhecido como Lapsus$ e também se envolveu em ataques contra Uber, Revolut e BT/EE, com danos estimados em £ 10 milhões . Hacker que invadiu Rockstar usando um Fire Stick e vazou GTA 6 se declara culpado
Por Gabriel Cavalheiro | •
Em julgamento realizado nesta segunda-feira (16), o hacker responsável pelo vazamento de GTA 6 em 2022, Arion Kurtaj, declarou-se culpado por invadir e vazar clipes inacabados, além de tentar extorquir a Rockstar. Ele fazia parte do grupo hacker conhecido como Lapsus$ e também se envolveu em ataques contra Uber, Revolut e BT/EE, com danos estimados em £ 10 milhões.
O jovem de 21 anos havia sido sentenciado a uma estadia por tempo indeterminado em um hospital de segurança máxima, devido à gravidade do seu autismo. Em janeiro, no entanto, Kurtaj foi transferido para uma prisão comum após ser considerado apto para enfrentar o julgamento, conforme reportagem da BBC.
Além do ataque hacker às empresas, o réu foi acusado pela promotoria de desempenhar um papel de liderança no Lapsus$, gangue que também teria roubado US$ 300.000 de vítimas individuais. Além disso, durante a sua invasão à Uber, Kurtaj postou a foto de um pênis como parte das tentativas de extorquir a companhia para que a empresa pagasse o resgate.
Kurtaj se declarou culpado de todas as acusações, incluindo agressões físicas a trabalhadores enquanto estava sob custódia, entre elas, múltiplos incidentes envolvendo mordidas. O jovem será sentenciado em uma data posterior.
Como foi o ataque hacker de GTA 6 em 2022?
Kurtaj invadiu a Rockstar Games em 2022, aos 16 anos. Na ocasião, ele estava hospedado no Hotel Travelodge em Bicester, Reino Unido, sob fiança por outros crimes cibernéticos e proteção policial. Ele recebeu ameaças de hackers rivais que tiveram seus estoques de bitcoin roubados pelo adolescente.
Mesmo com o computador confiscado, Kurtaj conseguiu invadir os sistemas da Rockstar apenas com um Amazon Fire Stick, a TV do hotel, um teclado e um mouse Bluetooth. A empresa se recusou a pagar o resgate dos dados obtidos pelo jovem.
Em setembro de 2022, o hacker vazou 90 arquivos com 60 minutos de gameplay de GTA 6, além de parte do código-fonte do jogo. Kurtaj também conseguiu invadir o Slack da produtora. As informações revelaram a existência de Lucia como a primeira protagonista feminina de um jogo de GTA em 3D, algo até então desconhecido.
 "Recentemente, sofremos uma invasão de rede, em que um terceiro não autorizado acessou e baixou ilegalmente informações confidenciais de nossos sistemas, incluindo imagens do desenvolvimento inicial para o próximo Grand Theft Auto. Agora, não planejamos nenhuma interrupção nos nossos serviços de jogos online nem qualquer efeito de longo prazo no desenvolvimento dos nossos projetos em andamento", escreveu a empresa em comunicado na época.
Segundo a Rockstar, o ataque custou cerca de US$ 5 milhões à companhia, além de milhares de horas de trabalho da equipe.
Hackers protagonizam a história de GTA 6
A invasão de Kurtaj resultou nas primeiras informações públicas sobre GTA 6. Quatro anos mais tarde, o hacker conhecido como Cyberleek protagonizou outro caso parecido e, desta vez, vazou dezenas de clipes de gameplay que revelaram uma lista de recursos presentes no jogo final. O ataque aconteceu pouco antes de o trailer do jogo estrear na Netflix.
Apesar da futura condenação de Arion Kurtaj e do sumiço de Cyberleek, a Rockstar e a Sony ainda correm contra o tempo, já que um hacker desbloqueou o PS5 na versão exigida por GTA 6.
